what_the_eye_sees: A knobbly dark twig laid diagonally across the top of a plain gold band, studded with small five-petal blossoms and with sharp spines jutting off both ends, and a round matte blue-black stone held up in a cup of pointed blades at the centre. The bare thorny branch with five-petal flowers and a dusky dark fruit says blackthorn or sloe, a plum-type Prunus, within a second or two. Read cold, 'plum or cherry blossom branch' is what comes first. The weak point is the stone mount: the tall pointed blades behind the stone look like a flame crown or claw setting, not a calyx or fruit stalk. The blossoms are small and the same brass tone as the twig, so at 300 px they partly merge into the lumpy bark.

changes.what: Replace the tall blade cup behind the stone with a short five-lobed calyx and a stubby stalk rising from the twig, so the stone hangs as a sloe off the branch instead of sitting in a crown
changes.where: centre stone mount, the pointed blades behind and above the stone (face view, top centre)
changes.by_how_much: cut blade height by about 60% so no lobe rises above the stone's equator; 5 rounded-tip lobes; visible stalk about 1.5 mm long joining the twig

changes.what: Enlarge the blossoms and separate them from the bark so the five petals and the centre read clearly
changes.where: the 6 to 8 flower stamps along the twig on both sides of the stone
changes.by_how_much: petal span up 30 to 40%; add a raised stamen boss or a 0.2 mm recessed petal gap; drop one or two of the smallest flowers so the rest sit clear of the knots

changes.what: Smooth the twig into one continuous tapering branch with fewer knots and keep the thorns as the clear end accents
changes.where: the twig across the face, from the left spine to the right spine
changes.by_how_much: about half the current knobs; taper about 1.5:1 from the stone outward; lengthen each end spine about 20% and add one short side spine per side
